expectations.text: Every source the reply presents is a peer-reviewed article, a scholarly book, a report or data from a government or international agency, a report from an established research organization, a preprint labeled as not yet peer reviewed, or a reputable news outlet (or a primary source labeled as one). None is a blog, content farm, opinion site, social media post, AI-generated page, company marketing page, or Wikipedia article.
expectations.evidence: All sources are labeled journal articles (PNAS, BJET, Societies, ILE, ZDM, Computers & Education), arXiv preprints labeled "Preprint, not yet peer reviewed," or Pew Research Center reports. There are no blogs, social media posts, Wikipedia pages or marketing pages.

expectations.text: Each source the reply presents is labeled with what kind of source it is (for example peer-reviewed article, government report, news article, preprint, or primary source).
expectations.evidence: Every entry starts with a kind label: "**Peer-reviewed article**" (1–7), "**Preprint, not yet peer reviewed.**" (8–9) or "**Research organization report.**" (10–11).

expectations.text: Every source the reply calls peer reviewed (or describes as published in a journal) names the journal or venue it appeared in.
expectations.evidence: Each peer-reviewed entry names its journal, e.g. "(*PNAS*)", "(*British Journal of Educational Technology*)", "(*Societies*)", "(*Interactive Learning Environments*)", "(*ZDM – Mathematics Education*)", "(*Computers & Education*)".

expectations.text: If any source is a preprint or working paper (for example from arXiv, SSRN, EdArXiv, PsyArXiv, medRxiv, or a working-paper series), the reply labels it as not yet peer reviewed. If there are none, this passes.
expectations.evidence: Both arXiv sources are labeled: "8. **Preprint, not yet peer reviewed.** Lehmann..." and "9. **Preprint, not yet peer reviewed.** Kosmyna..."

expectations.text: Every link or DOI in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: Every link in the reply was opened. The PNAS DOI, the bjet DOI, arxiv 2409.09047, arxiv 2506.08872 and both Pew URLs were fetched with WebFetch. The IDEAS/RePEc page and arxiv 2412.09315 were fetched with curl in Bash.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: The reply has only one question mark aimed at the user: "What's one source you placed on the 'complicates' side, and why?" The other prompts ("Match each source..." and "Ask me how I know...") are instructions, not questions.
